Memphis Milano leaflet

Christoph Radl’s 1983 Memphis leaflet: a catalogue grid of lamps under a row of labelled pattern swatches.

Source
Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam: Memphis Milano (2010.1.0622(1-4))
Creator
Christoph Radl (designer); Sottsass Associati (client); Memphis (publisher); Occhipinti (printer)
Made
1983
Style
Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Graphic, catalogue, loud, systematic
Evidence
Downloaded the museum’s published image (500 × 364 px) from the Stedelijk Museum to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The object has four parts; the image shows one side of one part. The record classes it as graphic design and does not say “leaflet”; that word is the catalogue’s description from the image and the 34.2 × 98.5 cm size.
Reviewed
25 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Stedelijk lists Christoph Radl as designer, Sottsass Associati as client, Memphis as publisher, and Occhipinti as printer; 1983; 34.2 × 98.5 cm; four parts. Stedelijk record.

Interni says Radl began working with Ettore Sottsass in 1980, “designing the image of Memphis”, and later curated the 2022 Triennale exhibition “Memphis Again”. Interni: Memphis Again.

Observed

  • A top row of pattern swatches is labelled by designer, name, and year, for example Nathalie Du Pasquier “Gabon” 1982 and Ettore Sottsass “Rete” and “Schizzo”.
  • The swatches include black-and-white nets and squiggles and bright color prints in pink, blue, yellow, and red.
  • A black band carries the “MEMPHIS MILANO” wordmark in blocky white letters.
  • Below, a grid of numbered photographs on black shows lamps by Bedin, Thun, Sottsass, De Lucchi, and others, each captioned with name and year.

Why it belongs

The leaflet treats patterns as products: laminates and textiles get the same captioned cells as lamps. For a website, the grid shows a way to lay out a Memphis catalogue without losing order.

Borrow

Put pattern swatches in a strict captioned grid so the pattern is loud but the layout stays calm.

Use black cells behind product photographs so saturated objects stand out.

Pattern shown here: Gabon. Wordmark study: Radl’s logotype drawing.
